nfl.oneThing: Josh Jacobs comes off the commissioner's exempt list on Monday and is eligible to play next week, but the league's investigation is still open and a suspension remains possible.

headlines.title: Josh Jacobs back from exempt list, but suspension still possible
headlines.summary: Josh Jacobs will be removed from the commissioner's exempt list on Monday, which makes him eligible to practise and play next week. The league's personal conduct investigation is still ongoing, so a suspension is still possible. Jacobs has already missed the first six games, and those count toward any suspension. If he is suspended for more than six games, he would miss further games to make up the difference. The Packers (3–2) play the Cowboys at Lambeau Field this Sunday before visiting the Lions on Oct. 25.

headlines.title: Eagles lose Jalen Hurts to blood clot, sign Joe Milton
headlines.summary: Jalen Hurts has been shut down for the immediate future with a superficial blood clot in his calf. The Eagles say it was suffered in their Oct. 4 game against the Rams. He was cleared to play against the Jaguars on Oct. 11, but a follow-up ultrasound showed movement in the clot. Philadelphia has signed Joe Milton III off the Cowboys' practice squad and added him to the active roster, and Tanner McKee is slated to start. Saquon Barkley is out with a hamstring injury, Will Shipley has gone on injured reserve, and DeVonta Smith is expected back against the Panthers.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Eagles are 2–3 and ranked No. 11 in the NFC, so the quarterback and backfield changes come at a tough point in their season.

headlines.title: Jonathon Cooper cleared to return in Week 7
headlines.summary: The NFL removed Broncos edge rusher Jonathon Cooper from the commissioner's exempt list on Friday, so he is eligible to play in Week 7. He had been on the list since Aug. 30. The Broncos veteran is their starting edge rusher, and his teams must still decide whether he is ready to play. Denver is 4–2 and ranked No. 6 in the AFC.
headlines.whyItMatters: A starting edge rusher returning would add depth to a Broncos defence that is already in the playoff picture.

headlines.title: Caleb Williams questionable for Falcons game
headlines.summary: Caleb Williams is listed as questionable for the Bears' Week 6 game at Atlanta. He has missed three straight games with a hamstring injury, and he was a full participant in practice on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. He still has to clear several medical protocols before the team leaves for Atlanta. Coach Ben Johnson said he hopes to have more clarity before then. Chicago is 3–2 and ranked No. 7 in the NFC after a loss to the Packers.
headlines.whyItMatters: A clean bill of health would return the Bears' starting quarterback to a team that is in the playoff picture at 3–2.

teamNews.title: Tonka Hemingway out, Jalen Nailor expected back
teamNews.text: Silver and Black Pride reports defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway will not play against the Bills after missing the week with a concussion. Adam Butler and Jonah Laulu should get more snaps, and Jalen Nailor is expected to play after missing last week. The injury report lists Nailor as questionable. Kubiak said Dont'e Thornton and Carter Runyon will not be activated from injured reserve this week, although Runyon has been designated to return.

teamNews.title: Tre Tucker's season-high snap count
teamNews.text: Tre Tucker played 75 percent of the snaps in the 45–17 loss at New England, the most on the team that day and a season high for him. He finished with four catches for 41 yards.

contextCard.title: How the commissioner's exempt list works
contextCard.body: The commissioner's exempt list keeps players away from games and practice while the league handles a matter, such as an investigation. It is separate from injured reserve. The league removes a player from the list, but the player's team still decides whether he is ready to return to play.

nba.oneThing: Jimmy Butler is targeting a return between January and February after tearing his right ACL, and the Warriors have not offered him in trade talks since the injury.

headlines.title: Butler targets January or February return from ACL tear
headlines.summary: Jimmy Butler could return from his torn right ACL between January and February, team sources told ESPN. He tore the ligament on Jan. 19 against the Heat. Before the injury he was having a resurgent season, averaging 20 points a game. Golden State went 12–26 without him and reached the Play-In as the No. 10 seed, where it lost to Phoenix in a blowout. Butler says he feels he let Steph Curry, Draymond Green and Steve Kerr down, and he wants to make that right.
headlines.whyItMatters: A return in January or February would give Golden State a major boost, after it went 12–26 without him last season.

headlines.title: Basket Zaragoza challenges Aday Mara's NBA eligibility
headlines.summary: Basket Zaragoza of Spain says Thunder rookie Aday Mara is still under contract with the club for 2026–27, and it is challenging his eligibility to play in the NBA this season. The Thunder dispute the claim and point to guidance from the NBA. Mara played for the Spanish club before three seasons of college basketball. The Thunder are 1–4 in the preseason.
headlines.whyItMatters: The result decides whether one of the Thunder's rookies can play this season.

headlines.title: Buss siblings push back in Lakers sale fight
headlines.summary: Joey and Janie Buss asked a Los Angeles judge on Friday to dismiss Jeanie Buss' claim that the family trust cannot sell the remaining Lakers shares without her consent. Their filing ran to 29 pages. Jeanie, the Lakers' acting governor, filed a 97-page petition in August. Five of the siblings are also challenging her petition to oust them as trustees.
headlines.whyItMatters: The court's decision could determine whether the family's last Lakers stake can be sold.

headlines.title: Bucks move home opener for World Series Game 1
headlines.summary: The Bucks moved their home opener against the Bulls up four hours, to 3pm CT on Oct. 23. That avoids a clash with Game 1 of the World Series in Milwaukee. It is the Brewers' first World Series trip in 44 years, after they clinched the NL pennant with a sweep of the Dodgers on Oct. 15. The NBA approved the change.
headlines.whyItMatters: It's a rare schedule change for a sporting moment in the same city, and the Bucks open their season in the afternoon as a result.
